text:
incident-bot: Automated alert: increased inference 5xxs + tail latency in eu-west-1a (az1a). Trigger: grpc_stream_error_rate > 5% for 10m. Creating incident channel and paging oncall.

.dave-oncall: I got the page, jumping in. Starting triage.

.ben-sre: seeing lots of short-lived TCP resets from a subset of hosts in az1a. Packet counters show NIC RX/TX spikes then drops. Likely intermittent NIC firmware hiccup or driver path.

.carol-eng: confirming from autoscaler: request queue on inference replicas in az1a spiked and then many requests retried -> 502/504. Telemetry shows KV-cache latency spike too.

.dave-oncall: mitigation plan (short): 1) Drain affected instance pool in az1a (evict new queries), 2) Shift routing away from az1a to eu-west-1b/c asap, 3) Lower LB healthcheck grace to fail-fast for flaky targets, 4) Notify customers on impacted API keys.

.ben-sre: executing drain now: `./tools/drain-pool --region eu-west-1a --pool inference-ephemeral` -> started. Also flipped traffic policy to prefer eu-west-1b with `routing-policy set prefer:eu-west-1b fallback:eu-west-1c`.

.frank-telemetry: confirming reroute: outbound % tokens served from eu-west-1a -> 12% (was 68%) in last 90s. Error rate per-route down from 6.8% -> 1.9%. Latency tail still elevated for inflight requests (p95->p99).

.carol-eng: running a quick probe against a degraded host, logs:
``` 
2026-03-17T12:04:02Z error grpc: stream error: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection reset by peer
2026-03-17T12:04:03Z warn net: nic rx queue dropped packets: count=12457
2026-03-17T12:04:04Z info kvcache: miss_latency_ms=240
```
Looks like NIC RX queue 'flashback' causing connection stickiness/failures.

.eva-support: Customer impact: Support routing shows ~8 customers reported elevated 5xxs (partial failures for multipart streaming). Two larger customers (acct: redwood-fin, acct: ad-creative) saw retries and user-facing errors. I've opened support tickets and posted a brief status note.

.dave-oncall: good. I'll escalate to infra for firmware/host investigation but for product impact we must keep traffic out of az1a until we confirm stability. Setting incident severity -> SEV2.

.ben-sre: coordinating with cloud provider: raised ticket w/ AWS (ref# 0A-9999) referencing NIC firmware anomalies on host fleet. Meanwhile we've increased cross-AZ reserved capacity by spinning up 10 extra inference replicas in eu-west-1b/c and bumped autoscaler min for dedicated pools.

.alice-oncall: taking 15:00-17:00 UTC oncall window. Dave handing off. Anything I should watch?

.dave-oncall: handoff notes: az1a NICs showing intermittent RX drops, drain in-progress, routing shifted, LB grace lowered to 2s, support notified, AWS ticket opened. Keep an eye on token distribution and error rate for streaming endpoints. If errors >2% for 10m, re-open paging.

.alice-oncall: acked. I'll monitor and follow up with infra for host-level remediation and potential live kernel/firmware updates.

.frank-telemetry: creating checkpoint graphs and saved alert state. Will attach p95/p99 + cross-AZ token share to the incident doc.

.eva-support: posted customer update: "We're mitigating an infrastructure networking issue in one AZ that caused partial inference failures; traffic is being shifted to healthy AZs and we're monitoring. ETA next update 30m."

.dave-oncall: thanks team. Leaving channel to infra and next oncall. Marking immediate mitigation complete; continuing root cause follow-up. :white_check_mark:
